{
  "needed": true,
  "prompt": "Goal
- For ordinary (non-superuser) users, any GET / PUT / DELETE request that targets another user's existing item must return HTTP 404 with JSON body {"detail": "Item not found"}. The same exact response must be returned when the item truly does not exist. This must not change owner/superuser permissions or listing behavior: owners and superusers retain their original permissions; list endpoints continue to return only the data the current user is allowed to see (do not expand visibility). Frontend will treat 404 as "not found" and must not learn about other users' resources.

High-level approach (framework-agnostic)
1. Define a single canonical 404 response payload constant: {"detail": "Item not found"} and use it everywhere for both "not found" and "forbidden because owned by someone else" cases.
2. Centralize object fetch + visibility check in one helper (or dependency/mixin/middleware) so controllers/handlers use the same behavior and message.
   - Behavior of the helper: try to load the item by id; if item == null -> raise/return canonical 404. If item exists but item.owner != current_user and current_user is not superuser -> raise/return canonical 404. Otherwise return the item.
   - Do NOT return 403 or other error types for "exists but not owned"; always use the same 404 payload.
3. Use that helper in all single-item endpoints (GET detail, PUT/PATCH update, DELETE). Do NOT expose raw lookup results before the permission check.
4. Preserve existing owner/superuser semantics: the helper must allow access if current_user is the owner OR current_user has superuser privileges (or other original elevated privileges if present). Do not change any logic granting elevated access.
5. Do NOT change list endpoints to expose other users' items. Keep the existing filtering for list endpoints (usually filter by current user or by existing visibility rules). Do not return other users' resources in lists.
6. Add tests that assert identical 404 responses for (a) non-existent id, (b) existent id owned by another ordinary user. Also tests for owner and superuser behavior (owner allowed, superuser allowed if previously allowed), and list behavior unchanged.
7. Avoid leaking information in logs or error headers. Log internally as needed, but the HTTP response must always be the canonical 404 body in the two scenarios above.

Detailed implementation checklist (apply to your stack)
A. Create canonical error
- Add a constant, e.g. NOT_FOUND_PAYLOAD = {"detail": "Item not found"} and use it for all relevant 404 responses.

B. Implement centralized fetch-or-404-with-visibility helper
- Signature example (conceptual):
  get_item_or_404_if_not_visible(model, id, current_user) -> item or raise 404 with NOT_FOUND_PAYLOAD
- Steps inside helper:
  1) item = db.get_by_id(model, id)
  2) if item is None: raise/return 404 with NOT_FOUND_PAYLOAD
  3) if item.owner_id != current_user.id and not current_user.is_superuser:
       raise/return 404 with NOT_FOUND_PAYLOAD
  4) return item

C. Use the helper in single-item endpoints
- For GET detail: call helper; if it returns item -> serialize and return normal 200; otherwise helper already returned 404 with canonical payload.
- For PUT/PATCH: call helper first. If allowed, perform update and return normal success code (200/204) as before. Do not do owner checks again unless there are additional ownership rules.
- For DELETE: call helper first. If allowed, perform delete and return previous success code as before.

D. Ensure list endpoints are unchanged
- Do not switch list endpoints to return other users' items. Keep the existing filter logic. If lists were previously restricted to the current user's visible items, do not broaden that. If there is already superuser behavior for lists, do not change it.

E. Tests to add/modify
- Test: ordinary user A requests GET /items/{id} for item owned by user B -> response status 404 and body EXACTLY {"detail": "Item not found"}.
- Test: ordinary user A requests GET /items/{nonexistent_id} -> same 404 and payload.
- Test: ordinary user A requests PUT/DELETE for item owned by user B -> same 404 and payload.
- Test: owner requests GET/PUT/DELETE on their own item -> original success behavior unchanged.
- Test: superuser requests GET/PUT/DELETE on other user's item -> original permission behavior unchanged (allowed if that was previously allowed).
- Test: list endpoint returns only visible items (unchanged from existing behavior).

F. Logging and observability
- Internally, log an appropriate event if necessary, but do not include any different response text or status that would reveal whether the requested id existed or who owned it. The HTTP response must always be the canonical 404 payload in both "not exists" and "exists but not permitted" cases.

Concrete code patterns (pick one matching your stack)
- Django REST Framework (override get_object)
  1) Define NOT_FOUND_PAYLOAD = {"detail": "Item not found"}
  2) In your ModelViewSet / GenericAPIView subclass, override get_object():
     def get_object(self):
         lookup_url_kwarg = self.lookup_url_kwarg or self.lookup_field
         pk = self.kwargs[lookup_url_kwarg]
         try:
             obj = self.queryset.get(pk=pk)
         except Model.DoesNotExist:
             raise NotFound(detail=NOT_FOUND_PAYLOAD)
         # visibility check
         user = self.request.user
         if getattr(obj, 'owner_id', None) != getattr(user, 'id', None) and not getattr(user, 'is_superuser', False):
             raise NotFound(detail=NOT_FOUND_PAYLOAD)
         return obj
  3) Use this get_object for retrieve/update/destroy actions. Do not call permission classes that convert the same case into 403; prefer this get_object approach so response is 404.

- FastAPI (dependency)
  1) Define NOT_FOUND_PAYLOAD = {"detail": "Item not found"}
  2) Create dependency:
     async def get_item_or_404(id: int, current_user: User = Depends(get_current_user)):
         item = await db.get_item(id)
         if item is None:
             raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Item not found")
         if item.owner_id != current_user.id and not current_user.is_superuser:
             raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Item not found")
         return item
  3) Use this dependency in GET/PUT/DELETE endpoints for the path parameter. For example:
     @router.get("/items/{id}")
     async def read_item(item: Item = Depends(get_item_or_404)):
         return item

- Express.js / Node (middleware)
  1) const NOT_FOUND_RESPONSE = { detail: 'Item not found' }
  2) async function fetchVisibleItem(req, res, next) {
       const id = req.params.id
       const user = req.user
       const item = await db.findItemById(id)
       if (!item) return res.status(404).json(NOT_FOUND_RESPONSE)
       if (item.ownerId !== user.id && !user.isSuperuser) return res.status(404).json(NOT_FOUND_RESPONSE)
       req.item = item
       next()
     }
  3) Attach fetchVisibleItem to GET/PUT/DELETE routes and use req.item inside handlers.

Checklist before deploy
- All single-item endpoints use centralized helper or equivalent to return canonical 404 for missing or unauthorized-by-ownership.
- List endpoints remain unchanged in visibility filtering.
- Unit/integration tests cover both missing and unauthorized-by-ownership returning identical 404 JSON payload.
- Verify superuser/owner original behaviors are unchanged.
- Confirm logs do not leak existence information to clients.

Notes and cautions
- Do not return 403 for ownership-based denial; returning 403 would reveal resource existence. The requirement mandates a 404 for both cases.
- Do not alter non-ownership authorization rules unrelated to this requirement (unless you intentionally centralize them in the helper and keep semantics identical for superusers/owners).
- If there are additional elevated roles beyond 'superuser' in your system, treat them as before: allow access if those roles previously allowed access (do not downgrade them). Ensure the helper checks for whatever elevated-privilege flags your system uses.

Deliverables to produce
- Implementation patch that introduces the helper/dependency/mixin and updates all single-item endpoints to use it.
- Automated tests described above.
- Short integration test demonstrating unchanged list response for current user and 404 behavior for other-user item accesses."
}
